groups.title: Testing philosophy and the testing pyramid
groups.question: Your team has no tests and wants to start. Explain which kinds of tests to write for a full-stack app and what to fake versus run for real.

followUps.Unit, integration, and E2E tests: cost v: What are the trade-offs between unit, integration and end-to-end tests?
followUps.What to mock and what to test for real: Why mock an email service but use a real database in integration tests?

evidence.text: Unit tests are fast and cheap but test pieces in isolation.
Integration tests use real parts like the database and give more confidence.
End-to-end tests drive a real browser through the app and catch the most but are slow, so there should be few.
External services like email or payment APIs are mocked because they are slow, cost money or are outside your control.
A real test database catches SQL and ORM bugs that a mock would hide.
Mocking too much makes tests pass while the real system fails.

groups.title: Playwright's browser automation model
groups.question: Your browser tests fail randomly because they click buttons before they appear, and someone added sleep calls to fix it. Explain how Playwright avoids this.

followUps.Playwright's auto-wait: how it retries a: How does Playwright's auto-waiting make tests less flaky than fixed sleeps?

evidence.text: Playwright waits for an element to be visible, enabled and stable before acting on it.
Its assertions retry until they pass or time out.
This removes the need for fixed sleeps, which are both slow and unreliable.

groups.title: Writing tests for the full stack
groups.question: You are writing tests for a recipe service function and for the POST /recipes endpoint with validation and auth. Explain how you would structure and write them.

followUps.Jest unit tests: describe, it, beforeEac: How do describe, beforeEach and matchers help organize unit tests?
followUps.Supertest for Express endpoint integrati: What does Supertest let you test that a unit test does not?

evidence.text: describe groups related tests together.
beforeEach sets up fresh state before each test, so tests do not affect each other.
Matchers like toEqual and toThrow state exactly what is expected.
Supertest sends real HTTP requests to the Express app in the same process.
The whole request pipeline runs, including validation, auth middleware and database writes.
Tests check the status code and response body, such as 401 without a token and 201 when valid.

groups.title: React component testing and E2E with Playwright
groups.question: You need tests for a recipe form component and for the login-and-create-recipe flow in a real browser, without tests breaking on every UI tweak. Explain how you would write them.

followUps.React Testing Library: query by role, in: Why query by role and use userEvent in component tests?
followUps.Playwright page object model for maintai: What is a page object and why use one in end-to-end tests?

evidence.text: Queries by role and name find elements the way users and screen readers do.
userEvent simulates realistic typing and clicking, including focus and keyboard events.
Tests written this way survive refactors of markup and class names.

notEnough: Only saying you use Testing Library.

evidence.text: A page object wraps the selectors and actions of one page in a class.
Tests read like steps, such as logging in and creating a recipe.
When the UI changes, selectors are updated in one place.
